title: K-flat realization of the augmented derived scalar-extension tower
statement:
Let $C$ be a site small in the module universe, $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $a_n:R\to B_n$ and $b_n:B_{n+1}\to B_n$ maps of sheaves of commutative rings for $n\ge1$, with $b_na_{n+1}=a_n$ [def-weil-inverse-system]. Use sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their unbounded derived categories and localizations $Q_R,Q_{B_n}$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $F_n=-\otimes_R^L B_n$, $G_n=-\otimes_{B_{n+1}}^L B_n$ for K-flat derived scalar extension [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], and $r_n:D(B_n)\to D(R)$, $j_n:D(B_n)\to D(B_{n+1})$ for exact scalar restriction [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Give these functors the normalized derived tensor/restriction adjunctions $F_n\dashv r_n$ and $G_n\dashv j_n$ of [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]; let $u_n:\mathrm{id}\to r_nF_n$ be their units. Let $\alpha_n:G_nF_{n+1}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_n$ be the canonical scalar-composition comparison [lem-sfb-successive-derived-quotient-normalization]. For $K\in D(R)$ let $\delta_n(K):F_{n+1}K\to j_nF_nK$ be the adjoint of $\alpha_n(K)$. Define $d_n(K):r_{n+1}F_{n+1}K\to r_nF_nK$ by applying $r_{n+1}$ to $\delta_n(K)$ and using the identity-on-underlying-sheaves comparison $r_{n+1}j_n\cong r_n$.

Let $P$ be a K-flat $R$-complex with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] and $e:Q_R(P)\xrightarrow{\sim}K$ an isomorphism. Put $T_n(P)=\operatorname{Res}_{a_n}(P\otimes_RB_n)$, using sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], with strict maps $t_n(p\otimes b)=p\otimes b_n(b)$ and $c_n(p)=p\otimes1$. The canonical K-flat computation comparisons, transported along $F_n(e^{-1})$ and then restricted, give isomorphisms
$$\epsilon_n:r_nF_nK\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_R(T_n(P))$$
satisfying
$$\epsilon_n\circ u_n(K)\circ e=Q_R(c_n),\qquad
\epsilon_n\circ d_n(K)=Q_R(t_n)\circ\epsilon_{n+1}.$$
These comparisons are natural for chain maps between flat-term K-flat representatives and respect every composite quotient transition. No flatness or surjectivity of $a_n$ or $b_n$, and no boundedness of $P$, is assumed.

source.place: Tag 06YY, lemma-derived-base-change; Tag 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition. Agent refinement retaining the K-flat computation comparisons, derived adjunction units and quotient transition maps simultaneously.

proof.text: Use the specified ordinary adjunction unit and ordinary tensor-composition formula in the normalization. Their composite sends s tensor x to b(s) tensor x; restrictionComp is the identity on sections. This proves the ordinary transition formula and preservation of the ordinary augmentation. Morphisms from a restricted scalar extension are determined by their pure sections: transport by obj_eq, forget to abelian sheaves, use sheafify_hom_ext, and apply tensor induction. Thus ordinary transitions preserve identities and compose according to composition of coefficient maps.

The computed field of the normalization makes the universal counit invertible on P. Mapping it under exact restriction and composing with right_factors gives the canonical computation isomorphism. The final identity-composition comparison in computation is the identity. Mapping e inverse and composing preserves invertibility. The adjunction_normalization field identifies the unit followed by computation with the localized ordinary unit. Naturality of the derived unit at e and e composed with e inverse equal to the identity prove the augmented equation.

Apply K-flat pullback preservation to the identity ringed topos and coefficient map a. It proves that the ordinary extension of P is K-flat with flat terms, so adjunction_normalization applies to the next coefficient map b.

For arbitrary a,b,a prime with a followed by b equal to a prime, substitute the equality. Expand derivedStep. Naturality of rightComp moves the universal counit across the restriction comparison. The representative field replaces the derived scalar-composition comparison followed by its counit with the two successive counits and the ordinary composition comparison. Naturality of the b-adjunction unit moves the first counit to the front. Rewrite rightComp_normalization, naturality of right_factors for b, the normalized b-unit on the extended P, and naturality of right_factors for a. The remaining equality in the homotopy category is the image of the termwise definition of ordinaryStep. Hence derivedStep followed by computation equals computation followed by the localized ordinaryStep. Naturality of derivedStep at e inverse proves the transported transition equation.

Naturality of the universal counit, right_factors and the induced homotopy-composition comparison proves computation natural for every chain map. From Q(f) followed by e prime equal to e followed by g, cancel the representative isomorphisms to obtain g followed by e prime inverse equal to e inverse followed by Q(f). Functoriality and computation naturality give the asserted naturality of epsilon.

Build a natural transformation between the inverse-sequence functors from the adjacent epsilon squares. Its naturality proves the square for every finite composite. The coefficient maps a themselves form a natural transformation from the constant sequence, giving the equation for the composite coefficient map. Induction on n less than or equal to m, using the identity law and the ordinaryStep pure-section formula with pure-section extensionality, identifies the direct ordinary mate with the ordinary finite composite. Apply the general computation square to the composite coefficient map and cancel the invertible epsilon at n to identify the direct derived mate with its finite composite. The base case uses empty composites and identities, so m equals n is included.
